title: The Brain Implant That Let a Paralyzed Man Type With His Mind 🤯
script: A paralyzed man typed 90 characters per minute — using only his thoughts. In 2021, BrainGate researchers implanted two tiny electrode arrays into Dennis Egan's motor cortex. He imagined moving a pen. The implant read the neural signals. A decoder turned them into letters — faster than most people type on a phone. No movement. No voice. Just thought becoming text in real time. But here's what nobody can agree on: if a machine reads your thoughts to communicate, where does assistive technology end and mind surveillance begin?
search_summary: BrainGate 2021 brain implant let paralyzed man type 90 characters per minute using neural signals
comment_question: If a chip can read your thoughts to type, who owns what's in your head? 🤯

title: The Spy Who Decoded His Own Death Warrant 😱
hook_text: He read the order to kill him
script: He deciphered the coded message — and realized it was his own execution order. In 1779, American spy John Honeyman operated deep inside British-held New Jersey, feeding George Washington intelligence before the Battle of Trenton. His cover was so perfect that patriots branded him a traitor. Washington had him arrested, then secretly freed him overnight — and told nobody why. Honeyman died in 1822 still despised by half his neighbors. His true role stayed classified for nearly a century. Would you die a traitor to save your country? Which is why.
search_summary: American spy John Honeyman decoded his own execution order while working as a double agent before the Battle of Trenton 1776.
comment_question: Would you let your neighbors hate you forever to protect a secret? 🤔
source_note: Stryker, The Battle of Trenton and Princeton, 1898
